title: Ink on Scroll, Endless Rows, Diffed Type, Grab-Anywhere Folds & Declared Behaviour
description: Five patterns that let something else do the work: the scroll timeline, a measured loop, a diff, one crease line, and the markup itself.

drops.title: Ink That Draws on Scroll
drops.description: A container names a view-timeline and every SVG path hangs its stroke-dashoffset on it — no scroll listener anywhere.
drops.concept: Scroll-driven animation finally makes draw-on-scroll a declaration rather than a tween loop. The container declares view-timeline-name, each path animates stroke-dashoffset against it with its own staggered animation-range, and a registered @property --p exposes the same progress to captions, lifts and meters. A JS engine using IntersectionObserver and getTotalLength stands by for browsers without it — and the panel lets you force it to compare.
drops.source: DhruvilChauahan0210/ink-scroll — scroll-driven SVG drawing in ~10 KB, zero deps

interaction.mouse: Scroll the page; each figure inks itself across its own slice of the timeline.
interaction.click: Toggle the JS fallback engine, or retime the whole page from the panel.
interaction.touch: Scroll works identically; the panel hides on small screens.

drops.title: Three Rows That Never Land
drops.description: Four copies of each sequence, a measured loop period, and a wrap you cannot see — drag it, fling it, or leave it drifting.
drops.concept: An endless editorial gallery built from three masked rows on one centred stage, each with its own height, opacity, scale, direction and drag weight. The loop period is measured as the distance between the same slot in two consecutive copies, so the wrap is exact after any resize. Drag moves all three with different weights, release flings them with decaying momentum, and the idle drift fades back in about three-quarters of a second later.

interaction.mouse: Drag anywhere to move all three rows; the wheel adds to the same velocity.
interaction.click: Nothing to click — the stage is one big drag surface.
interaction.touch: Touch-drag and fling are the primary input; reduced motion stops the drift.

drops.title: Only What Changed Moves
drops.description: Grapheme atoms, an LCS diff, hunks: matched runs glide with FLIP and never re-render, only the edits travel in.
drops.concept: Most text transitions crossfade the whole string, which throws away the fact that most of it did not change. Here both strings are split into grapheme atoms with Intl.Segmenter, diffed with a zero-dependency LCS, and grouped into hunks — matched runs shorter than minChunk are demoted unless they are whole words. Matched atoms glide with FLIP; changed hunks travel, scale and de-blur in on a stagger, optionally merging through an SVG alpha-threshold goo filter.
drops.source: ehsania/rtl-text-transform — goo and changed-hunk rise text morphs

interaction.mouse: Step the headline, post a new meter reading, and watch which glyphs refuse to move.
interaction.click: Buttons drive each demo; the panel tunes travel, blur, stagger and the minimum matched run.
interaction.touch: Type into the third demo — every keystroke is its own diff.

drops.title: The Page Folds Where You Grab It
drops.description: The crease is the perpendicular bisector of where you grabbed and where you are — clip one side, reflect the other.
drops.concept: A page turn that only works from the corner quietly tells readers where to put their hand. This one derives the fold line from two points instead: grab anywhere, and the crease is the perpendicular bisector of the grab point and the pointer. The sheet is clipped to one half-plane with clip-path, the other half is reflected across the crease to become the leaf, and a gradient whose first stop sits exactly on the crease carries the bend. Release past the commit threshold and the turn finishes itself.
drops.source: javocsoft/grabfold — a page-turn you can grab anywhere

interaction.mouse: Drag any sheet from any point on it; release short to spring back, past the threshold to turn.
interaction.click: A tap without a drag flicks the page from the right edge.
interaction.touch: Touch-drag works the same; reduced motion turns instantly.

drops.title: Behaviour Declared in the Markup
drops.description: Tabs, accordion, dialog and switch share one binder that only ever reads data-slot and writes data-state.
drops.concept: Headless components usually arrive as a framework. Here the structure is the configuration: every part names itself with data-slot, the root carries its options as data attributes, and a single 60-line create() scan wires keyboard navigation, ARIA and focus trapping. The script never creates an element or sets a style — it writes data-state, and the stylesheet does the rest. Flipping data-type on the accordion changes its behaviour with no rebinding.
drops.source: bejamas/data-slot — vanilla JS behaviour primitives for accessible components

interaction.mouse: Click tabs, accordion rows, the dialog trigger and the switches.
interaction.click: Arrow keys, Home/End, Space, Enter and Escape are all wired from the same scan.
interaction.touch: Everything is tap-sized; the live data-state inspector hides on small screens.
